audit_scope.description: This audit covers EL block validation (EIP-7934), CL data availability sampling (PeerDAS/DAS Core), P2P networking changes (EIP-8070 eth/71 sparse blobpool), and Fusaka fork meta-coordination (EIP-7607).

out_of_scope: Fork Choice (not covered by these subgraphs)
Attestation logic (not covered by these subgraphs)

out_of_scope_reasons.JSON-RPC API: Vulnerabilities requiring the user to have publicly exposed an API are explicitly out-of-scope
out_of_scope_reasons.Beacon API: Vulnerabilities requiring the user to have publicly exposed an API are explicitly out-of-scope
out_of_scope_reasons.Infrastructure bugs: Webpages, DNS, email, etc. are out-of-scope
out_of_scope_reasons.High-effort DoS attacks: Sustained, CPU or bandwidth intensive, and/or requires more than 1 packet or on-chain transaction
out_of_scope_reasons.Non-Fusaka vulnerabilities: Should be submitted via the Ethereum Foundation's Bug Bounty Program
out_of_scope_reasons.Publicly known issues: All TODO/FIXME/BUG/HACK items and publicly known issues are not eligible

misclassified_entities.reason: Client implementation teams are a governance/operational entity, not a runtime external data source that sends data into the system. Not relevant to trust boundary analysis.
Network operators are an operational entity, not a runtime external data source. Not relevant to trust boundary analysis.
Core developers are a governance entity involved in EIP scheduling, not a runtime external data source.
EIP authors are a governance entity, not a runtime external data source.

trusted_external_entities.name: P2P Peer via Gossip (DataColumnSidecar)
trusted_external_entities.rationale: P2P peers are unauthenticated. Any node can join the network and send arbitrary DataColumnSidecar messages on gossip subnets. All data must be fully validated (format, inclusion proof, KZG proofs) before acceptance.

trusted_external_entities.name: P2P Peer via Req/Resp (Column Requests)
trusted_external_entities.entry_point: Req/Resp protocol for missing column data requests
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Peers responding to direct column requests are unauthenticated. Responses may contain invalid or withheld data. KZG proof verification is required on all received column data.

trusted_external_entities.name: P2P Peer via devp2p (Block Propagation)
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Peers propagating blocks are unauthenticated. Blocks may be oversized or malformed. RLP size validation (EIP-7934: MAX_RLP_BLOCK_SIZE = 8 MiB) must occur early before expensive processing.

trusted_external_entities.name: P2P Peer via eth/71 (Sparse Blobpool Messages)
trusted_external_entities.entry_point: eth/71 protocol messages (NewPooledTransactionHashes 0x08, GetPooledTransactions 0x09, PooledTransactions 0x10, GetCells 0x12, Cells 0x13)
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Peers sending eth/71 messages are unauthenticated. All message types (announcements with cell_mask, cell requests/responses) must be parsed and validated. Malicious peers may send invalid cell_mask bitmaps, return partial or invalid cell data, or attempt selective withholding attacks.

trusted_external_entities.name: Provider Peer (Sparse Blobpool)
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Provider peers claim to have full blob data but are unauthenticated. Noise column verification (C_extra=1 random column) is used to detect selective withholding, but a coordinated attacker controlling all providers could bypass detection. Provider role is determined probabilistically (p=0.15) and cannot be externally verified.

trusted_external_entities.name: Malicious Validator via P2P
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Archetypal CL attack vector. A malicious validator can propose invalid blocks, submit conflicting attestations, or withhold blob data columns to disrupt data availability.

trusted_external_entities.name: Consensus Layer via Engine API
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Authenticated via JWT. Co-located CL client sends execution payloads for validation. While the channel is authenticated, payload content must still be validated (e.g., block size limits apply). A compromised or buggy CL could send invalid data.

trusted_external_entities.name: Execution Layer via Engine API
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Authenticated via JWT. Co-located EL client returns blob data and execution results. Some data (e.g., blob data from engine_getBlobsV2) may be used without KZG verification by the CL, creating a trust gap if the EL is compromised.

trusted_external_entities.name: User via Transaction Submission
trusted_external_entities.entry_point: On-chain transactions (type-3 blob transactions, standard transactions)
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Archetypal EL attack vector. Users submit transactions that enter the mempool and may be included in blocks. Transactions must be fully validated (signature, gas, nonce, size constraints). Blob transactions introduce additional validation via EIP-7594 and sparse blobpool mechanics.

boundary_edges.security_assumption: All received DataColumnSidecars must be validated: (1) column index within [0, NUMBER_OF_COLUMNS), (2) cell count matches expected, (3) commitment_inclusion_proof valid against signed block header, (4) KZG cell proofs valid against commitments. Reject and penalize peer on failure.
Column data received via Req/Resp must undergo identical validation as gossip-received data (format, inclusion proof, KZG proofs). Missing or invalid responses should trigger peer scoring penalties.

RLP-encoded block size must be checked against MAX_RLP_BLOCK_SIZE (8,388,608 bytes) early in the validation pipeline, before expensive operations like signature verification. Oversized blocks must be rejected immediately.

All eth/71 messages must be parsed and validated: cell_mask must be nil when no type-3 TXs or valid B_16 bitmap, GetCells requests must be bounded (max C_req=8 columns), Cells responses must match requested data. Malformed messages should trigger peer disconnection.

Provider responses must include the noise column (C_extra=1 random column). Missing noise column indicates potential selective withholding. Cell data must be validated per EIP-7594. At least 2 distinct providers must be observed before sampling.

JWT authentication must be verified. Execution payloads must still be validated against EL rules including EIP-7934 block size limits. Engine API is a semi-trusted boundary: authentication is verified but content validation is still required.

boundary_edges.target_component_interface: Engine API engine_getBlobsV2 / execution payload response
boundary_edges.security_assumption: JWT authentication must be verified. Blob data returned via engine_getBlobsV2 should ideally be KZG-verified by CL, but current specs may not require this. A compromised EL could return corrupted blob data that propagates to the network.

boundary_edges.target_component_interface: Transaction pool ingestion (via P2P or local submission)
boundary_edges.security_assumption: Full transaction validation required: signature verification, gas limit checks (EIP-7825 transaction gas limit cap), nonce validation, blob transaction validation per EIP-7594. Type-3 blob transactions require additional KZG commitment verification.

Block proposals must be fully validated: proposer signature, slot validity, state transition correctness. Blob data availability must be confirmed via PeerDAS sampling before attestation. Conflicting attestations must trigger slashing conditions.
